# Purpose

This notebook estimates the response of national GDP-per-capita growth to
temperature and precipitation on PWT 11.0 x ERA5 (population-density weights,
base year 2000), from 1970 to the last PWT year:

1. the BHM level specification, with and without the conflict and collapse
   controls and the 1991-1993 growth outliers;
2. three forms of the weather deviation from each country's mean over that
   horizon, in SDs over the same horizon: signed, linear arms and quadratic arms;
3. the same three forms with the deviation from the trailing 20-year mean, in
   trailing 20-year SDs;
4. quadratic arms with the temperature deviation as in 2 and the precipitation
   deviation as in 3.

Every model has year and country fixed effects and country linear trends, with
errors clustered by country. Sections 2 to 4 use the same sample (controls
included, outliers dropped), so their fit statistics are comparable.

# Setup

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
required_packages <- c("arrow", "countrycode", "dplyr", "fixest", "ggplot2", "knitr", "readxl",
                       "tibble", "zoo")
missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]
if (length(missing_packages)) {

    "Install missing packages before running this notebook: ",
    paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

## Shared specification

```{r shared-specification}
ECON_DATA <- "PWT"
CLIMATE_SOURCE <- "ERA5"
CLIMATE_WEIGHT <- "population density"
CLIMATE_WEIGHT_YEAR <- 2000L
START_YEAR <- 1970L

outcome <- "dlgrp_pc_usd"
fixed_effects <- "year + GID_1 + GID_1[year]"

# The UCDP/PRIO conflict indicators by the highest intensity of the country's
# conflicts that year (functions/conflict.R): conflict_low, minor (25-999
# battle deaths), and conflict_high, war (1,000 or more).
CONFLICT_TERMS <- c("conflict_low", "conflict_high")
# The conflict indicators and the post-Soviet (with Albania) and post-Yugoslav
# collapse-year dummies (functions/transition_collapse.R).
CONTROLS <- c(
  CONFLICT_TERMS,
  "i(fsu_collapse_year, ref = 'none')",
  "i(yug_collapse_year, ref = 'none')"
)

# Growth outliers of the post-Pinatubo years: the 2.5% largest growth shocks
# (growth net of the fixed effects and the controls) that fall in 1991-1993.
OUTLIER_YEARS <- 1991:1993
OUTLIER_SHARE <- 0.025

fit_model <- function(terms, model_data) {
  fit_panel_model(
    paste(terms, collapse = " + "),
    model_data,
    outcome = outcome,
    fixed_effects = fixed_effects,
    cluster = ~GID_0
  )
}

# Labels for the coefficient tables; the collapse dummies are left out of them.
DICT <- c(
  TM = "T", TM2 = "T^2", RR = "P", RR2 = "P^2",
  conflict_low = "Conflict, minor", conflict_high = "Conflict, war",
  mean_TM_all = "mean T", mean_RR_all = "mean P",
  devTM = "dT", devTM_pos = "dT+", devTM_neg = "dT-",
  devTM_pos2 = "(dT+)^2", devTM_neg2 = "(dT-)^2",
  devRR = "dP", devRR_pos = "dP+", devRR_neg = "dP-",
  devRR_pos2 = "(dP+)^2", devRR_neg2 = "(dP-)^2"
)
DROP <- "collapse_year"
# Temperature terms, then precipitation terms, then the controls (original names).
ORDER <- c("%^devTM", "%^devRR", "%^conflict")
FITSTAT <- ~n + wr2 + aic + bic
```

# Data

The climate panel starts well before 1970, so `mean_TM_all`, `sd_TM_all`,
`mean_RR_all` and `sd_RR_all` from `build_dat()` (each country's entire climate
series) are replaced here by the moments over the horizon of the analysis:

```text
mean_TM_all, sd_TM_all = mean and SD of TM over 1970 .. last PWT year
mean_RR_all, sd_RR_all = mean and SD of RR over 1970 .. last PWT year
```

taken from the climate series of every year in that horizon, whether or not the
country has PWT growth that year.

```{r build-data}
panel_cfg <- panel_config(
  econ_year_min = START_YEAR,
  climate_source = CLIMATE_SOURCE,
  climate_weight = CLIMATE_WEIGHT,
  climate_weight_year = CLIMATE_WEIGHT_YEAR,
  # One earlier year carries the lagged trailing moments into 1970.
  clim_history_years = 1L
)
data <- build_dat(econ_data = ECON_DATA, config = panel_cfg)
END_YEAR <- max(data$year[est_row(data)])

horizon_moments <- load_climate_panel("gadm0", panel_cfg) %>%
  filter(gadm_level == "gadm0", year >= START_YEAR, year <= END_YEAR) %>%
  group_by(GID_1) %>%
  summarise(
    years_TM = sum(!is.na(TM)),
    years_RR = sum(!is.na(RR)),
    mean_TM_all = mean(TM, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_TM_all = sd(TM, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_RR_all = mean(RR, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_RR_all = sd(RR, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

data <- data %>%
  select(-c(mean_TM_all, sd_TM_all, mean_RR_all, sd_RR_all)) %>%
  left_join(select(horizon_moments, -years_TM, -years_RR), by = "GID_1")

data <- add_yugoslav_collapse(add_soviet_collapse(add_conflict(data)))
data$TM2 <- data$TM^2
data$RR2 <- data$RR^2
```

Horizon: `r START_YEAR`-`r END_YEAR` (`r END_YEAR - START_YEAR + 1` years).
Countries with climate in fewer years than that:
`r sum(horizon_moments$years_TM < END_YEAR - START_YEAR + 1 | horizon_moments$years_RR < END_YEAR - START_YEAR + 1)`.

## Sample and outliers

One sample for every model: country-years from `r START_YEAR` with growth,
both weather variables, the conflict indicators, and the moments of both
deviation definitions (positive SDs). The outliers are flagged once on this
sample, net of the fixed effects and all the controls.

```{r sample}
moments <- c(
  "mean_TM_all", "sd_TM_all", "mean_RR_all", "sd_RR_all",
  "mean_TM_lag_20", "sd_TM_lag_20", "mean_RR_lag_20", "sd_RR_lag_20"
)
needed <- c(outcome, "TM", "RR", CONFLICT_TERMS, moments)
complete <- stats::complete.cases(as.data.frame(data)[, needed])
positive_sd <- Reduce(`&`, lapply(grep("^sd_", moments, value = TRUE), function(x) {
  !is.na(data[[x]]) & data[[x]] > 0
}))
sample_all <- data[est_row(data) & data$year >= START_YEAR & complete & positive_sd, ]

outliers <- flag_growth_outliers(
  sample_all, CONTROLS, fixed_effects, OUTLIER_YEARS, OUTLIER_SHARE
)
sample_clean <- sample_all[!outliers$flag, ]

tibble::tibble(
  sample = c("all", "outliers dropped"),
  observations = c(nrow(sample_all), nrow(sample_clean)),
  countries = c(n_distinct(sample_all$GID_0), n_distinct(sample_clean$GID_0)),
  first_year = c(min(sample_all$year), min(sample_clean$year)),
  last_year = c(max(sample_all$year), max(sample_clean$year))
) %>%
  knitr::kable()

sample_all %>%
  count(conflict_intensity, name = "country_years") %>%
  mutate(conflict = c("none", "minor (25-999 deaths)", "war (1,000+)")[conflict_intensity + 1],
         countries = vapply(conflict_intensity, function(k) {
           n_distinct(sample_all$GID_0[sample_all$conflict_intensity == k])
         }, 0L)) %>%
  select(conflict, country_years, countries) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Country-years by the highest conflict intensity of the year")

outliers$table %>%
  mutate(across(c(growth, growth_shock, shock_cutoff), ~ round(100 * .x, 1))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Dropped outliers (growth and shock in pp)")
```

# BHM levels: controls and outliers

The BHM specification in levels:

```text
growth = b1 TM + b2 TM^2 + b3 RR + b4 RR^2 [+ controls] + year + country + country trend
```

with the two conflict indicators (minor, war) alone, then with the collapse
dummies too, without the outliers, and with both (the specification of the
sections below).

```{r bhm-levels}
bhm_terms <- c("TM", "TM2", "RR", "RR2")
m_bhm <- list(
  fit_model(bhm_terms, sample_all),
  fit_model(c(bhm_terms, CONFLICT_TERMS), sample_all),
  fit_model(c(bhm_terms, CONTROLS), sample_all),
  fit_model(bhm_terms, sample_clean),
  fit_model(c(bhm_terms, CONTROLS), sample_clean)
)

etable(
  m_bhm,
  headers = c("Baseline", "Conflict", "Conflict + collapse", "Outliers dropped",
              "Controls, outliers dropped"),
  dict = DICT,
  drop = DROP,
  extralines = list(
    "Collapse dummies" = c("No", "No", "Yes", "No", "Yes"),
    "Outliers dropped" = c("No", "No", "No", "Yes", "Yes")
  ),
  fitstat = FITSTAT
)

# Temperature at which the marginal effect of temperature is zero, -b1 / (2 b2),
# and the joint Wald test of both temperature terms.
tibble::tibble(
  model = c("Baseline", "Conflict", "Conflict + collapse", "Outliers dropped",
            "Controls, outliers dropped"),
  turning_point_C = vapply(m_bhm, function(m) -coef(m)[["TM"]] / (2 * coef(m)[["TM2"]]), 0),
  temperature_wald_p = vapply(m_bhm, function(m) {
    fixest::wald(m, keep = "^TM2?$", print = FALSE)$p
  }, 0)
) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ signif(.x, 3))) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

# Deviations from the horizon mean

The deviation of each variable from its mean over the horizon, in SDs over the
horizon, and its terms:

```text
dT   = (TM - mean_TM_all) / sd_TM_all          (same for precipitation, dP)
dT+  = max(dT, 0)        dT-  = max(-dT, 0)
```

Each form enters with its interaction with the long-run climate (the horizon
mean), for both variables, plus the controls; outliers dropped:

```text
signed          growth = a dT  + b dT  x mean_TM_all + (same in dP) + controls + FE
linear arms     growth = a+ dT+ + a- dT- + (b+ dT+ + b- dT-) x mean_TM_all + (same in dP) + controls + FE
quadratic arms  growth = a+ (dT+)^2 + a- (dT-)^2 + (b+ (dT+)^2 + b- (dT-)^2) x mean_TM_all + (same in dP) + controls + FE
```

```{r deviation-terms}
# Deviation terms against the moments mean_<v>_<mean_suffix> and
# sd_<v>_<sd_suffix>; a suffix is either common to both variables or named by
# variable, e.g. c(TM = "all", RR = "lag_20"). The same column names under any
# definition, so the tables line up.
add_deviation_terms <- function(model_data, mean_suffix, sd_suffix) {
  for (v in c("TM", "RR")) {
    mean_v <- if (length(mean_suffix) > 1) mean_suffix[[v]] else mean_suffix
    sd_v <- if (length(sd_suffix) > 1) sd_suffix[[v]] else sd_suffix
    dev <- (model_data[[v]] - model_data[[paste0("mean_", v, "_", mean_v)]]) /
      model_data[[paste0("sd_", v, "_", sd_v)]]
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v)]] <- dev
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_pos")]] <- pmax(dev, 0)
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_neg")]] <- pmax(-dev, 0)
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_pos2")]] <- pmax(dev, 0)^2
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_neg2")]] <- pmax(-dev, 0)^2
  }
  model_data
}

FORMS <- list(
  "Signed" = "",
  "Linear arms" = c("_pos", "_neg"),
  "Quadratic arms" = c("_pos2", "_neg2")
)
form_terms <- function(suffixes) {
  terms <- unlist(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    x <- paste0("dev", v, suffixes)
    c(x, paste0(x, ":mean_", v, "_all"))
  }))
  c(terms, CONTROLS)
}
fit_forms <- function(model_data) lapply(FORMS, function(s) fit_model(form_terms(s), model_data))
```

```{r horizon-deviations}
data_horizon <- add_deviation_terms(sample_clean, "all", "all")
m_horizon <- fit_forms(data_horizon)

etable(m_horizon, dict = DICT, drop = DROP, order = ORDER, fitstat = FITSTAT)
```

# Deviations from the trailing 20-year mean

The same forms, interactions (with the horizon mean) and sample, with the
deviation from the trailing 20-year mean (the 20 years before the current one),
in SDs over the same 20 years:

```text
dT = (TM - mean_TM_lag_20) / sd_TM_lag_20          (same for precipitation, dP)
```

A unit of dT is a different number of degrees under the two definitions, so
compare the coefficients across sections through their sign and pattern, and
the fit statistics directly.

```{r trailing-20-deviations}
data_20 <- add_deviation_terms(sample_clean, "lag_20", "lag_20")
m_20 <- fit_forms(data_20)

etable(m_20, dict = DICT, drop = DROP, order = ORDER, fitstat = FITSTAT)
```

## Comparison

```{r compare-definitions}
deviation_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(
  list("Horizon mean and SD" = data_horizon, "Trailing 20-year mean and SD" = data_20),
  function(x) {
    tibble::tibble(
      variable = c("Temperature", "Precipitation"),
      sd = c(sd(x$devTM), sd(x$devRR)),
      min = c(min(x$devTM), min(x$devRR)),
      max = c(max(x$devTM), max(x$devRR)),
      share_above_2 = c(mean(abs(x$devTM) > 2), mean(abs(x$devRR) > 2)),
      corr_with_horizon = c(cor(x$devTM, data_horizon$devTM), cor(x$devRR, data_horizon$devRR))
    )
  }
), .id = "deviation")
deviation_summary %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Distribution of the deviations over the sample (SD units)")

# Fit of each model (all on the same rows), and the joint Wald tests of each
# variable's terms.
fit_summary <- function(models) {
  tibble::tibble(
    form = names(models),
    observations = vapply(models, stats::nobs, 0),
    within_r2 = vapply(models, function(m) fixest::fitstat(m, "wr2")[[1]], 0),
    aic = vapply(models, stats::AIC, 0),
    bic = vapply(models, stats::BIC, 0),
    temperature_wald_p = vapply(models, function(m) {
      fixest::wald(m, keep = "^devTM", print = FALSE)$p
    }, 0),
    precipitation_wald_p = vapply(models, function(m) {
      fixest::wald(m, keep = "^devRR", print = FALSE)$p
    }, 0)
  )
}
# AIC and BIC relative to the best model of the table, rounded for display.
format_fit <- function(fit) {
  stopifnot(length(unique(fit$observations)) == 1)
  fit %>%
    mutate(
      aic_vs_best = aic - min(aic),
      bic_vs_best = bic - min(bic),
      within_r2 = round(within_r2, 4),
      across(c(aic, bic, aic_vs_best, bic_vs_best), ~ round(.x, 1)),
      across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))
    )
}

fit_table <- bind_rows(lapply(
  list("Horizon mean and SD" = m_horizon, "Trailing 20-year mean and SD" = m_20),
  fit_summary
), .id = "deviation")
format_fit(fit_table) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Fit and joint tests; AIC and BIC relative to the best of the six models")
```

# Mixed: horizon temperature, trailing 20-year precipitation

Quadratic arms for both variables, with the temperature deviation from the
horizon mean (in horizon SDs) and the precipitation deviation from the trailing
20-year mean (in trailing 20-year SDs); interactions with the horizon means,
controls and sample as above:

```text
dT = (TM - mean_TM_all) / sd_TM_all
dP = (RR - mean_RR_lag_20) / sd_RR_lag_20

growth = a+ (dT+)^2 + a- (dT-)^2 + (b+ (dT+)^2 + b- (dT-)^2) x mean_TM_all
       + c+ (dP+)^2 + c- (dP-)^2 + (e+ (dP+)^2 + e- (dP-)^2) x mean_RR_all
       + controls + FE
```

In the tables: Mixed, next to the quadratic-arms models with both deviations
from the horizon mean (Horizon) and both from the trailing 20-year mean (20-year).

```{r mixed-deviations}
data_mixed <- add_deviation_terms(
  sample_clean,
  mean_suffix = c(TM = "all", RR = "lag_20"),
  sd_suffix = c(TM = "all", RR = "lag_20")
)
m_quadratic <- list(
  "Horizon" = m_horizon[["Quadratic arms"]],
  "20-year" = m_20[["Quadratic arms"]],
  "Mixed" = fit_model(form_terms(FORMS[["Quadratic arms"]]), data_mixed)
)

etable(m_quadratic, dict = DICT, drop = DROP, order = ORDER, fitstat = FITSTAT)

format_fit(fit_summary(m_quadratic)) %>%
  rename(deviations = form) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Quadratic arms: fit and joint tests; AIC and BIC relative to the best of the three")
```

# Trailing climate mean and variability

Does a more variable recent climate lower growth? The quadratic-arms models with
both deviations from the trailing 20-year mean (20-year) and with the mixed
deviations (Mixed), adding as level regressors the trailing 20-year mean
temperature and the trailing 20-year SDs of temperature and precipitation (all
over the 20 years before the current one):

```text
growth = quadratic arms (as above) + controls + FE
       + m mean_TM_lag_20 + s_T sd_TM_lag_20 + s_P sd_RR_lag_20
```

`s_T`, `s_P` < 0 mean that growth is lower when the recent climate has been more
variable. With country effects and trends, all three are identified only from
their changes within countries beyond a linear trend, so the effects are also
given per within-country SD of each regressor (its residual SD after the fixed
effects).

```{r trailing-moments}
quadratic_terms <- form_terms(FORMS[["Quadratic arms"]])
MOMENT_TERMS <- c("mean_TM_lag_20", "sd_TM_lag_20", "sd_RR_lag_20")
MOMENT_SETS <- list(
  "Baseline" = character(0),
  "+ mean T" = "mean_TM_lag_20",
  "+ SDs" = c("sd_TM_lag_20", "sd_RR_lag_20"),
  "+ mean T + SDs" = MOMENT_TERMS
)
MOMENT_DATA <- list("20-year" = data_20, "Mixed" = data_mixed)
m_moments <- lapply(MOMENT_DATA, function(model_data) {
  lapply(MOMENT_SETS, function(x) fit_model(c(quadratic_terms, x), model_data))
})
MOMENT_DICT <- c(DICT, mean_TM_lag_20 = "mean T, trailing 20y (C)",
                 sd_TM_lag_20 = "SD T, trailing 20y (C)",
                 sd_RR_lag_20 = "SD P, trailing 20y (m)")
MOMENT_ORDER <- c("%^mean_TM_lag_20$", "%^sd_TM_lag_20$", "%^sd_RR_lag_20$", ORDER)

etable(m_moments[["20-year"]], title = "Both deviations from the trailing 20-year mean",
       dict = MOMENT_DICT, drop = DROP, order = MOMENT_ORDER, fitstat = FITSTAT)
etable(m_moments[["Mixed"]], title = "Mixed deviations",
       dict = MOMENT_DICT, drop = DROP, order = MOMENT_ORDER, fitstat = FITSTAT)

# Within-country variation of each moment: its residual SD after the fixed
# effects (year, country, country trends), on the estimation rows.
within_sd <- vapply(MOMENT_TERMS, function(x) {
  m <- fixest::feols(stats::as.formula(paste(x, "~ 1 |", fixed_effects)), data_mixed,
                     notes = FALSE)
  stats::sd(stats::resid(m))
}, 0)

bind_rows(lapply(names(m_moments), function(spec) {
  m <- m_moments[[spec]][["+ mean T + SDs"]]
  ct <- fixest::coeftable(m)[MOMENT_TERMS, , drop = FALSE]
  tibble::tibble(
    specification = spec, term = MOMENT_DICT[MOMENT_TERMS],
    estimate = ct[, 1], std_error = ct[, 2], p_value = ct[, 4],
    within_sd = within_sd[MOMENT_TERMS],
    effect_per_within_sd_pp = 100 * ct[, 1] * within_sd[MOMENT_TERMS],
    sds_joint_p = fixest::wald(m, keep = "^sd_(TM|RR)_lag_20$", print = FALSE)$p
  )
})) %>%
  mutate(across(c(estimate, std_error, within_sd), ~ signif(.x, 3)),
         across(c(p_value, sds_joint_p), ~ signif(.x, 2)),
         effect_per_within_sd_pp = round(effect_per_within_sd_pp, 3)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Trailing moments, last column of each table: effect on growth",
                               "of one within-country SD of each (pp)"))
```

# Binned responses

For each deviation definition above, the response to each variable's deviation
by quarter of its long-run climate (the quartiles of `mean_TM_all` and
`mean_RR_all` over the sample), against the signed and quadratic-arms forms
interacted with the long-run climate, as in the tables. Only the bins have
coefficients per quarter.

- Bins: 0.5 SD bins of the deviation within each quarter, centred on zero, with
  the tails pooled until they hold 10 countries; the bin containing zero is the
  quarter's reference. One model per variable: its bins, the other variable in
  signed + quadratic arms (interacted with its long-run mean), and the controls,

  ```text
  growth = sum over quarters q and bins k of  c_qk 1[dT in bin k of quarter q]
         + (a dP + a+ (dP+)^2 + a- (dP-)^2) + (b dP + b+ (dP+)^2 + b- (dP-)^2) x mean_RR_all
         + controls + FE
  ```

  and the same with temperature and precipitation swapped.
- Curves: the signed and quadratic-arms models of the sections above, estimated
  once over all countries with the interaction with the long-run climate (no
  quarter terms), e.g. for quadratic arms

  ```text
  growth = a+ (dT+)^2 + a- (dT-)^2 + (b+ (dT+)^2 + b- (dT-)^2) x mean_TM_all
         + c+ (dP+)^2 + c- (dP-)^2 + (e+ (dP+)^2 + e- (dP-)^2) x mean_RR_all
         + controls + FE
  ```

  and drawn at the quarter's mean long-run climate, relative to their mean over
  the quarter's reference-bin observations, to be on the bins' scale.

```{r binned-setup}
BIN_WIDTH <- 0.5
MIN_COUNTRIES <- 10L
VARIABLE_LABELS <- c(TM = "Temperature", RR = "Precipitation")
QUARTER_NAMES <- list(TM = c("coldest", "cool", "warm", "hottest"),
                      RR = c("driest", "dry", "wet", "wettest"))
CLIMATE_UNITS <- c(TM = "°C", RR = "m")
CLIMATE_DIGITS <- c(TM = 1L, RR = 2L)
# The other variable's terms in the bin models: signed + quadratic arms.
ENCOMPASSING <- c("", "_pos2", "_neg2")
PLOTTED_FORMS <- c("Signed", "Quadratic arms")

# Value of a deviation term (by column suffix) at deviations x.
term_value <- function(suffix, x) {
  if (suffix == "") return(x)
  switch(suffix, "_pos" = pmax(x, 0), "_neg" = pmax(-x, 0),
         "_pos2" = pmax(x, 0)^2, "_neg2" = pmax(-x, 0)^2)
}
interaction_name <- function(a, b, terms) {
  intersect(c(paste0(a, ":", b), paste0(b, ":", a)), terms)[[1]]
}
wrap_text <- function(x, width) paste(strwrap(x, width = width), collapse = "\n")

# Quarter of each variable's long-run climate and bins of its deviation within
# each quarter (ids "<quarter>_<index>"), with each bin's size and mean deviation.
add_quarter_bins <- function(model_data) {
  quarters <- list()
  bins <- list()
  for (v in names(VARIABLE_LABELS)) {
    climate <- model_data[[paste0("mean_", v, "_all")]]
    breaks <- stats::quantile(climate, seq(0, 1, 0.25), names = FALSE)
    quarter <- as.integer(cut(climate, breaks, include.lowest = TRUE))
    dev <- model_data[[paste0("dev", v)]]
    k_max <- ceiling((max(abs(dev)) + BIN_WIDTH / 2) / BIN_WIDTH)
    edges <- seq(-BIN_WIDTH / 2 - k_max * BIN_WIDTH, BIN_WIDTH / 2 + k_max * BIN_WIDTH,
                 by = BIN_WIDTH)
    bin <- character(nrow(model_data))
    for (q in 1:4) {
      rows <- quarter == q
      q_breaks <- pool_tails(dev[rows], edges, model_data$GID_0[rows], MIN_COUNTRIES)
      bin[rows] <- sprintf("%d_%02d", q, as.integer(cut(dev[rows], q_breaks,
                                                        include.lowest = TRUE)))
      reference <- sprintf("%d_%02d", q, as.integer(cut(0, q_breaks)))
      bins[[length(bins) + 1]] <- tibble::tibble(
        variable = v, quarter = q, bin = bin[rows], deviation = dev[rows],
        GID_0 = model_data$GID_0[rows]
      ) %>%
        group_by(variable, quarter, bin) %>%
        summarise(observations = n(), countries = n_distinct(GID_0),
                  mean_deviation = mean(deviation), .groups = "drop") %>%
        mutate(reference = bin == !!reference)
    }
    model_data[[paste0(v, "_quarter")]] <- quarter
    model_data[[paste0(v, "_bin")]] <- bin
    fmt <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = CLIMATE_DIGITS[[v]])
    # Outside tibble(), whose `quarter` column would mask the vector.
    mean_climate <- as.numeric(tapply(climate, quarter, mean))
    quarters[[v]] <- tibble::tibble(
      variable = v, quarter = 1:4, mean_climate = mean_climate,
      label = sprintf("%s, %s quarter\n%s to %s %s; curves at the mean, %s %s",
                      VARIABLE_LABELS[[v]], QUARTER_NAMES[[v]], fmt(breaks[-5]),
                      fmt(breaks[-1]), CLIMATE_UNITS[[v]], fmt(mean_climate),
                      CLIMATE_UNITS[[v]])
    )
  }
  list(data = model_data, quarters = bind_rows(quarters), bins = bind_rows(bins))
}

# Effect of the interacted form with `suffixes` of variable v at long-run
# climate m and deviations `devs`, relative to its mean over `ref_devs`.
form_curve <- function(model, v, suffixes, m, devs, ref_devs) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(model))
  G <- t(vapply(devs, function(x) {
    w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
    for (s in suffixes) {
      term <- paste0("dev", v, s)
      value <- term_value(s, x) - mean(term_value(s, ref_devs))
      w[[term]] <- value
      w[[interaction_name(term, paste0("mean_", v, "_all"), terms)]] <- value * m
    }
    w
  }, numeric(length(terms))))
  colnames(G) <- terms
  linear_combination(model, G) %>% mutate(deviation = devs)
}

# Bins by quarter of long-run climate against the interacted forms of
# PLOTTED_FORMS (the models of the tables, refitted on the same rows), both
# variables.
plot_binned_response <- function(model_data, title, deviation_note) {
  qb <- add_quarter_bins(model_data)
  d <- qb$data
  models <- lapply(FORMS[PLOTTED_FORMS], function(s) fit_model(form_terms(s), d))
  bins <- list()
  curves <- list()
  for (v in names(VARIABLE_LABELS)) {
    other <- setdiff(names(VARIABLE_LABELS), v)
    other_terms <- paste0("dev", other, ENCOMPASSING)
    references <- qb$bins %>% filter(variable == v, reference) %>% pull(bin)
    bin_term <- sprintf("i(%s_bin, ref = c(%s))", v,
                        paste0("'", references, "'", collapse = ", "))
    m_bins <- fit_model(c(bin_term, other_terms,
                          paste0(other_terms, ":mean_", other, "_all"), CONTROLS), d)
    prefix <- paste0(v, "_bin::")
    estimates <- tidy_fixest(m_bins) %>%
      filter(startsWith(term, prefix)) %>%
      mutate(bin = sub(prefix, "", term, fixed = TRUE))
    bins[[v]] <- qb$bins %>%
      filter(variable == v) %>%
      left_join(select(estimates, bin, estimate, conf_low, conf_high), by = "bin") %>%
      mutate(across(c(estimate, conf_low, conf_high), ~ ifelse(reference, 0, .x)))

    dev <- d[[paste0("dev", v)]]
    for (q in 1:4) {
      rows <- d[[paste0(v, "_quarter")]] == q
      ref_devs <- dev[rows & d[[paste0(v, "_bin")]] %in% references]
      grid <- seq(min(dev[rows]), max(dev[rows]), length.out = 100)
      m <- qb$quarters$mean_climate[qb$quarters$variable == v & qb$quarters$quarter == q]
      for (f in names(models)) {
        curves[[length(curves) + 1]] <-
          form_curve(models[[f]], v, FORMS[[f]], m, grid, ref_devs) %>%
          mutate(variable = v, quarter = q, form = f)
      }
    }
  }

  facet_of <- function(variable, quarter) {
    factor(qb$quarters$label[match(paste(variable, quarter),
                                   paste(qb$quarters$variable, qb$quarters$quarter))],
           levels = qb$quarters$label)
  }
  bins <- bind_rows(bins) %>%
    mutate(facet = facet_of(variable, quarter),
           across(c(estimate, conf_low, conf_high), ~ 100 * .x))
  curves <- bind_rows(curves) %>%
    mutate(facet = facet_of(variable, quarter), form = factor(form, levels = names(models)),
           across(c(estimate, conf_low, conf_high), ~ 100 * .x))

  ggplot() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_line(data = curves, aes(deviation, estimate, colour = form), linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_linerange(data = filter(bins, !reference),
                   aes(mean_deviation, ymin = conf_low, ymax = conf_high),
                   colour = GRID_INK, linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_point(data = bins, aes(mean_deviation, estimate, shape = reference),
               colour = GRID_INK, fill = "white", size = 2.2) +
    # Common axes across all panels.
    facet_wrap(~facet, nrow = 2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = grid_colours(names(FORMS))[names(models)], name = NULL) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 16, `TRUE` = 21),
                       labels = c(`FALSE` = "Deviation bin (95% CI)", `TRUE` = "Reference bin"),
                       name = NULL) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1, order = 1), shape = guide_legend(order = 2)) +
    labs(
      x = "Deviation (SD)",
      y = "Effect on growth that year (pp), relative to the reference bin",
      title = title,
      subtitle = wrap_text(paste0(
        deviation_note, " Top: temperature, by quarter of long-run temperature; bottom: ",
        "precipitation, by quarter of long-run precipitation. Bins of ", BIN_WIDTH,
        " SD centred on zero (points at the bin's mean deviation; tails pooled to ",
        MIN_COUNTRIES, " countries). Curves: the forms interacted with the long-run ",
        "climate, estimated on the whole sample (no quarter terms) and evaluated at the ",
        "quarter's mean long-run climate, relative to the reference bin. Common axes."), 175),
      caption = wrap_text(paste0(
        ECON_DATA, " x ", CLIMATE_SOURCE, ", ", CLIMATE_WEIGHT, " ", CLIMATE_WEIGHT_YEAR,
        " weights, ", START_YEAR, "-", END_YEAR, "; controls: conflict (minor, war), post-Soviet and ",
        "post-Yugoslav collapse dummies; ", nrow(outliers$table), " growth outliers of ",
        min(OUTLIER_YEARS), "-", max(OUTLIER_YEARS), " dropped. Fixed effects year + country + ",
        "country linear trends; errors clustered by country."), 175)
    ) +
    theme_results()
}
```

# Conflict effects by country size

Do small countries lose more growth in conflict years? With log total GDP and
log GDP per capita together, the conflict effects scaled with the population
part of GDP, not with income, so size is measured by population. The mixed
quadratic-arms model of section 4, with the conflict indicators interacted with
the previous year's log population:

```text
growth = climate terms (mixed quadratic arms) + collapse dummies
       + g1 conflict_low + g2 conflict_high + h x
       + k1 conflict_low * x + k2 conflict_high * x + FE
```

with `x` the log population of the previous year (PWT `pop`, millions) and, in
the last column, also the log real GDP per capita of the previous year
(income), to tell populous countries from rich ones.

Both are centred on their sample means, so `g1` and `g2` are the effects of
conflict in a country of mean log population (and income), and `k1`, `k2` > 0
mean that more populous (richer) countries lose less. The level terms `h x` are
needed: without them the interactions would also pick up the relation between
`x` and growth in every year.

The last column asks whether weather deviations hurt more in conflict years,
and more so in small countries: the population model plus the symmetric squared
deviations `dT^2` and `dP^2` (mixed definitions) interacted with each conflict
indicator and with population, with all their lower-order terms:

```text
     + sum over v in (dT, dP) of  [ a_v pop * v^2
                                  + b1_v conflict_low * v^2  + c1_v conflict_low * pop * v^2
                                  + b2_v conflict_high * v^2 + c2_v conflict_high * pop * v^2 ]
```

`v^2` itself is already in the model as the sum of its two quadratic arms.
`b` is the extra effect of a squared deviation in a conflict year in a country
of mean log population; `c` < 0 means that extra effect is more negative in
more populous countries, `c` > 0 that it is more negative in smaller ones.

```{r conflict-size}
# Population of the previous year, matched on calendar year.
pwt_pop <- readxl::read_excel(data_file(ECON_RAW_FILES[["PWT110"]]), sheet = "Data") %>%
  transmute(GID_0 = as.character(countrycode), year = as.integer(year) + 1L,
            lag_log_pop = log(as.numeric(pop)))
data_size <- data_mixed %>%
  left_join(pwt_pop, by = c("GID_0", "year")) %>%
  # The previous year's log GDP per capita, from the panel's level and growth.
  mutate(lag_log_gdp_pc = lgrp_pc_usd - dlgrp_pc_usd)
stopifnot(nrow(data_size) == nrow(data_mixed), !anyNA(data_size$lag_log_pop))
POPULATION_MEAN <- mean(data_size$lag_log_pop)
INCOME_MEAN <- mean(data_size$lag_log_gdp_pc)
data_size$population <- data_size$lag_log_pop - POPULATION_MEAN
data_size$income <- data_size$lag_log_gdp_pc - INCOME_MEAN
# Symmetric squared deviations (the sum of the two quadratic arms).
data_size$devTM_sq <- data_size$devTM^2
data_size$devRR_sq <- data_size$devRR^2

climate_terms <- setdiff(form_terms(FORMS[["Quadratic arms"]]), CONTROLS)
interacted <- function(x) c(x, paste0(CONFLICT_TERMS, ":", x))
# Conflict x population x squared deviation, with its lower-order terms.
squared_terms <- unlist(lapply(c("devTM_sq", "devRR_sq"), function(s) {
  c(paste0("population:", s), paste0(CONFLICT_TERMS, ":", s),
    paste0(CONFLICT_TERMS, ":population:", s))
}))
m_size <- list(
  "Baseline" = fit_model(c(climate_terms, CONTROLS), data_size),
  "Lagged pop." = fit_model(c(climate_terms, CONTROLS, "population"), data_size),
  "x pop." = fit_model(c(climate_terms, CONTROLS, interacted("population")), data_size),
  "x pop., x GDP pc" = fit_model(c(climate_terms, CONTROLS, interacted("population"),
                                   interacted("income")), data_size),
  "x pop. x d^2" = fit_model(c(climate_terms, CONTROLS, interacted("population"),
                               squared_terms), data_size)
)

etable(
  m_size,
  dict = c(DICT, population = "log pop.(t-1)", income = "log GDP pc(t-1)",
           devTM_sq = "dT^2", devRR_sq = "dP^2"),
  keep = c("%^conflict", "%population", "%income", "%_sq"),
  order = c("%^conflict_low$", "%^conflict_high$", "%^population$", "%^income$",
            "%^conflict_low:income", "%^conflict_high:income",
            "%^conflict_low:population$", "%^conflict_high:population$",
            "%^population:devTM", "%^conflict_low:devTM", "%^conflict_high:devTM",
            "%^conflict_low:population:devTM", "%^conflict_high:population:devTM",
            "%^population:devRR", "%^conflict_low:devRR", "%^conflict_high:devRR",
            "%^conflict_low:population:devRR", "%^conflict_high:population:devRR"),
  fitstat = FITSTAT,
  notes = "Climate terms (mixed quadratic arms) and collapse dummies in every column."
)

# Joint Wald tests of the squared-deviation terms of the last column.
m_squared <- m_size[["x pop. x d^2"]]
wald_terms <- function(pattern) {
  terms <- grep(pattern, names(stats::coef(m_squared)), value = TRUE)
  test <- fixest::wald(m_squared, keep = paste0("^", terms, "$"), print = FALSE)
  tibble::tibble(terms = length(terms), F_stat = test$stat, p_value = test$p)
}
bind_rows(
  "Conflict x d^2 and conflict x pop. x d^2, both variables" = wald_terms("^conflict_.*_sq$"),
  "Conflict x pop. x d^2, both variables" = wald_terms("^conflict_.*:population:.*_sq$"),
  "Conflict x pop. x dT^2" = wald_terms("^conflict_.*:population:devTM_sq$"),
  "Conflict x pop. x dP^2" = wald_terms("^conflict_.*:population:devRR_sq$"),
  "War x dT^2 and war x pop. x dT^2" = wald_terms("^conflict_high:.*devTM_sq$"),
  "War x dP^2 and war x pop. x dP^2" = wald_terms("^conflict_high:.*devRR_sq$"),
  .id = "null: terms = 0"
) %>%
  mutate(F_stat = round(F_stat, 2), p_value = signif(p_value, 2)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Joint Wald tests, last column (errors clustered by country)")

# Effect of each conflict type at the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles of x
# across the country-years in conflict (other centred variables at their mean).
in_conflict <- data_size$conflict_low == 1 | data_size$conflict_high == 1
effects_at <- function(model, x, x_mean, label) {
  at <- stats::quantile(data_size[[x]][in_conflict], c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9), names = FALSE)
  terms <- names(stats::coef(model))
  bind_rows(lapply(CONFLICT_TERMS, function(k) {
    G <- t(vapply(at, function(value) {
      w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
      w[[k]] <- 1
      w[[interaction_name(k, x, terms)]] <- value
      w
    }, numeric(length(terms))))
    colnames(G) <- terms
    linear_combination(model, G) %>%
      mutate(model = label, conflict = DICT[[k]], percentile = c("10th", "50th", "90th"),
             population_millions = signif(exp(at + x_mean), 2), .before = 1)
  }))
}
bind_rows(
  effects_at(m_size[["x pop."]], "population", POPULATION_MEAN, "x pop."),
  effects_at(m_size[["x pop., x GDP pc"]], "population", POPULATION_MEAN,
             "x pop., x GDP pc (at mean income)")
) %>%
  mutate(across(c(estimate, std_error, conf_low, conf_high), ~ round(100 * .x, 2))) %>%
  rename(effect_pp = estimate) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Effect of a conflict year on growth (pp, 95% CI) at percentiles",
                               "of the previous year's population among country-years in",
                               "conflict"))
```
